html:
The Quatsino are a Kwakwaka'wakw people of Quatsino Sound, a long inlet on the northwest coast of Vancouver Island, British Columbia, Canada. Today the Quatsino First Nation includes descendants of several groups who once had their own villages around the sound.

Like other Kwakwaka'wakw, they lived from salmon, halibut, shellfish and cedar, and held potlatches to mark names and rank. Their language is Kwak'wala. Their neighbours to the south are the Nuu-chah-nulth.
